title: perf(hs-connectors): zero-copy Mooncake transfer with checked status codes
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Speed up the Mooncake hidden-states backend by removing redundant host-side work on both ends:

- **One object per sample.** Tensor bytes (64-byte aligned) + a JSON manifest trailer are published with a single put instead of `put_tensor` × 2 + manifest put. Publication is atomic, so the "manifest written last" protocol and partial-sample cleanup go away.
- **Zero-copy transfers.** Each thread owns a staging buffer registered with Mooncake once. The producer copies DtoH straight into pinned staging on the connector's copy stream and calls `put_from`; the consumer calls `get_into`. This drops the per-sample pinned allocation, the `get_buffer` bounce buffer, and the GIL-held `new char[]` + memcpy inside `get_tensor`, and lets RDMA read/write registered memory directly.
- **Drop CRC32.** It cost two full CPU passes per sample (~144 ms each for a 587 MB K3 sample). #967 introduced it together with return-code checking; before #967 `setup`/`put_tensor` statuses were ignored, so a failed put could still publish the manifest. The issues caught during the K3 run are most plausibly from that path, since TCP and RDMA are already checksummed on the wire. Integrity now rests on checked status codes, the manifest shape/dtype/bounds checks, and the producer-side finite check. @fynnsu, can you confirm what the K3 run actually tripped on (checksum mismatch vs. non-finite vs. missing tensor)?
- **Check every status code.** `register_buffer`, `put_from`, `put`, `is_exist`, `get_size`, `get_into`, `remove`. Only negative values count as failures, because the size/length APIs return positive counts.
- **Backoff polling.** vLLM answers the HTTP request before the connector's put lands, so the consumer almost always slept one full 50 ms poll. Polling now starts at 1 ms and doubles up to the 50 ms cap.

The manifest version is bumped to 2, so producer and consumer must run the same version.

## Tests

Unit: `pytest tests/unit/hs_connectors tests/unit/train/test_data.py` (62 passed). The fake store now implements the pointer-based API and checks that transfers only touch registered memory. New cases cover negative statuses for every call, short reads, out-of-bounds manifests, staging reuse/growth, and the backoff schedule.

**Microbench** (real Mooncake 0.3.13, 587 MB sample = 8192 × 5 × 7168 bf16, i.e. the Kimi-K3 DSpark shape, median of 10 serial ops, payload verified byte-exact):

| path | put main → PR | get+delete main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| TCP, same host | 207 → 98 ms | 336 → 133 ms |
| RDMA (2×100G RoCE), same host | 227 → 42 ms | 227 → 39 ms |
| TCP, cross-node | 198 → 73 ms | 845 → 660 ms (wire-bound) |
| RDMA, cross-node | 208 → 40 ms (14.6 GB/s) | 253 → 38 ms (15.3 GB/s) |

**E2E A/B**: Qwen3-4B verifier (vLLM 0.30.0, 1 GPU) + DFlash trainer (2 GPUs), seq 8192, 150 steps, `tutorial_regen` data. Store-op latencies were recorded with temporary instrumentation that is not part of this PR. Step profile means skip the first 10 steps.

| metric | main rdma | PR rdma | main tcp | PR tcp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| put p50 / p90 (ms) | 23.2 / 40.6 | 4.3 / 8.8 | 20.7 / 36.9 | 7.1 / 15.8 |
| get p50 / p90 (ms) | 72.5 / 120.1 | 15.2 / 69.7 | 97.6 / 165.7 | 51.8 / 115.4 |
| round trip p50 (ms) | 195.9 | 154.9 | 219.6 | 184.6 |
| trainer fetch_ms | 32.6 | 17.1 | 27.5 | 5.3 |
| step_ms | 362 | 303 | 404 | 353 |

This small setup is compute-bound (fetch is 1–7% of a step) and each cell is a single run, so read the step-level numbers as directional. The per-op latencies are the clean signal, and they matter most for large verifiers such as K3, where one sample is ~0.6 GB.

title: feat(evaluate): add MRCR long-context benchmark support
body:
## Purpose

As requested in (the now-closed) #1107, this minimally adds `openai/mrcr`
as a long-context dataset option to the existing
inference performance evaluation path (`scripts/evaluate/evaluate.py`)
without introducing additional machinery.

MRCR measures speculative decoding acceptance and server performance on
long-context "needle in a haystack"-style prompts.

Because GuideLLM cannot replay a multi-turn conversation without
regenerating the intermediate assistant turns, each MRCR conversation is
**pre-rendered server-side** into a single-turn prompt: every row is sent
through the target server's root `/tokenize` endpoint (with the
conversation's `messages`, applying the server's chat template), then
`/detokenize`, yielding the exact prompt string the server would prefill
plus its token count. Rows are then rebucketed by rendered token count,
and each bucket runs through GuideLLM as a `/v1/completions` workload —
the fixed assistant turns are part of the prompt, so only the final
answer is generated.

The prompt rendering takes ~10 minutes for one needle count (800 prompts),
but the result is cached for subsequent benchmarks with the same target 
model. This initial wait is not ideal, but seems to be required if we want
to tap into the existing GuideLLM benchmark path.

New options (ignored for the standard dataset and SPEED-Bench, just as
`--subsets` is ignored for MRCR):

- `--mrcr-needles` — needle counts to test (default: `2,4,8`)
- `--mrcr-buckets` — context-length buckets, by number 1-8 or label
  (default: all buckets)
- `--mrcr-data-dir` — cache directory for rendered data
  (default: `./mrcr_data`; gitignored, reused across runs, keyed by
  served model)
- `--mrcr-max-samples` — row cap per bucket, for quick debugging runs

The eight buckets span 4,096–1,048,576 rendered tokens. Buckets above
the server's context limit are skipped with a warning. Each
(needle-count, bucket) pair runs as its own subset, labeled
`mrcr/<N>needle/<bucket>` in `acceptance.csv` (and `perf_results.csv`
in sweep mode). Invalid selections (bad needle counts, unknown buckets,
duplicates, max-samples < 1) are rejected at argparse time with
specific messages.

Rendered data is cached per model, so the one-time rendering cost
(~800 rows per needle count, parallelized over 24 workers) is only paid
on first use or when the served model changes.

## Tests

End-to-end against a vLLM server (vLLM 0.30.0, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`,
262,144-token context):

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
        --speculative-config '{"model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8,"method":"dspark"}' \
        --tensor-parallel-size 2
```

```
$SPECULATORS_DIR/.venv/bin/python \
     ./scripts/evaluate/evaluate.py \
     --target http://localhost:8000/v1 throughput \
     --dataset openai/mrcr \
     --mrcr-needles 2
```

title: feat(eval): throughput mode via one mixed recorded run
body:
## Summary

Reimplements the **`throughput`** mode on the recorded-table harness introduced by #1107, so all subsets run **at once** in a single max-concurrency pass and acceptance is sliced out per subset afterward.

> **Stacked on #1107** — assumes it merges first. GitHub can't base an upstream PR on a fork branch, so this targets `main` and its commit list currently also shows #1107's two commits; those drop out automatically once #1107 merges, leaving only the throughput commits here. **Review only `throughput.py` + the `evaluate.py`/`acceptance_report.py` throughput wiring.**

### Why

The legacy `throughput` path ran each subset (`HumanEval`, `qa`, ...) through a **separate** guidellm pass and read acceptance off the server's **global** Prometheus counters, diffed before/after. A shared global counter can't be attributed to a subset while other subsets are in flight, so the subsets were **forced to run sequentially** — N isolated passes to measure N subsets.

Here every request carries its subset in `metadata`, and every response's *raw* per-request `speculative_decoding` block is recorded to the Parquet table. So all subsets can be **mixed into one saturated run** and sliced apart offline by `metadata.subset` — one pass instead of N, and the same recording yields both per-subset acceptance and an aggregate throughput figure.

### Design

Same three-layer split as #1107; only a new thin adapter is added:

- **`throughput.py` — thin adapter** (mirrors `mrcr.py`). Loads each subset's `<subset>.jsonl`, deterministically samples `--max-requests` records per subset by stable content hash (`sha256(seed + subset + prompt)`), tags each request with its subset + source-row pointer + a short prompt preview, mixes all subsets by a stable hash of the request id, and hands them to the generic runner with `fit_test=False` (prompts are short — no render fit-test needed; prompt length comes from the response usage block). No inference, persistence, or acceptance math lives here.
- **`request_runner.py` / `acceptance_report.py`** — reused unchanged, except `SpecRecord` now also carries the request's `metadata` (so acceptance can be grouped by subset).

Each request is tagged with its **`source_index`** (its row position in `<subset>.jsonl`, not the sampled order) plus a **`prompt_sha`**, so any offline report recovers the full prompt with a direct `jsonl[source_index]` lookup that self-checks against dataset drift — no fragile re-run of the sampler.

### Outputs

- `acceptance_by_subset.csv` + a printed table — requests, draft acceptance rate, and mean acceptance length per subset.
- `throughput_summary.json` — total ok requests, completion tokens, wall time, output tok/s, req/s across the whole mixed run.
- With `--top-n-prompts N`: prints the N best- and N worst-acceptance prompts per subset (a preview stored in `metadata` makes the printed report need no dataset reload; full prompts are recoverable offline via `source_index`).

### CLI

```bash
# Server needs detailed per-request metrics (no render endpoint required):
vllm serve <model> --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed \
    --speculative-config '{"model":"<draft>","num_speculative_tokens":N}'

# Mix all 9 standard subsets into one concurrent run, 200 samples each:
python evaluate.py --target http://localhost:8000/v1 throughput --max-requests 200

# Also print the 3 best/worst-acceptance prompts per subset:
python evaluate.py --target http://localhost:8000/v1 throughput --top-n-prompts 3
```

New/changed flags: `--max-new-tokens` (per-request generation cap), `--top-n-prompts` (best/worst report, default 0). `--selection-seed` is promoted from long-context-only to a general flag shared by both modes. `--max-requests` doubles as samples-per-subset for throughput.

SPEED-Bench throughput (`--dataset speedbench/...`) keeps the legacy guidellm path — its data isn't the standard subset layout. `sweep` is unchanged.

### Validation

Ran end-to-end against **Qwen3-8B + a DFlash speculator** (`num_speculative_tokens=7`, `--max-model-len 40960`) over all 9 standard subsets = **924 requests**, at 128 max-concurrency: deterministic subset-tagged selection, a Parquet table written, per-subset acceptance + aggregate throughput produced, and the best/worst report recovering full prompts by `source_index` (0 sha mismatches).

**New mixed run vs. the legacy per-subset guidellm path** — identical 924 records, identical 4096-token generation cap:

| | Legacy (9 sequential guidellm passes) | This PR (one mixed run) |
|---|---|---|
| Requests | 924 | 924 |
| Wall clock | 694 s | **561.9 s** |
| Wall tok/s | 1,972 | **2,404** |

**~1.24× faster wall-clock (−19%, 132 s saved).** The legacy path's *summed* active guidellm windows alone are 610 s — already longer than this PR's entire 562 s wall — and that excludes the ~84 s of inter-pass overhead (9× process startup + Prometheus counter diffing + per-pass ramp/drain tails). The small 80-request subsets can't fill 128-concurrency and each pays a startup+drain tail; mixing all subsets into one saturated stream overlaps those tails and keeps the server pinned.

**Cost of `--per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed`** — same workload against a server launched *without* the flag (throughput-normalized, since non-deterministic sampling makes each run's total token count differ by ~1%):

| | with flag | without flag |
|---|---|---|
| Output tok/s | 2,404 | 2,338 |

The ~3% gap is within run-to-run noise, and directionally the *flagged* run was nominally faster (which can only be noise, since the flag only adds server work). **The per-request-metrics overhead is below the measurement noise floor — negligible.**

title: feat(eval): long-context acceptance benchmark on a recorded request table
body:
## Summary

Adds a **`long-context`** evaluation mode that measures speculative-decoding acceptance as context length grows, using [OpenAI's MRCR dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr) as a source of long, multi-turn prompts.

The design principle: **a benchmark is just a set of requests to make (in some order, with an optional stop rule); everything is recorded to a table, and reports are pure functions over that table.** So the pieces are decoupled into three layers, none of which is MRCR-specific except the last:

1. **`request_runner.py` — generic runner.** Given an ordered set of requests (chat messages + sampling budget + opaque `metadata`) and an optional per-batch stop predicate, it renders each request through the server's own render endpoint (exact prompt length + context fit-test), generates whatever fits, and streams one flat row per request to a **Parquet table**: request identity, metadata, exact prompt length, response text, and the *raw* server metrics blob — all verbatim. It knows nothing about bins, context length, or spec-decode. Each batch is a separate Parquet part file, so a crash only loses the batch in flight.
2. **`acceptance_report.py` — spec-decode analysis over the table.** Context-length bucket edges live here as *analysis parameters*, not harness constants. Reports acceptance (a) by prompt length at request start and (b) by running token position within each request.
3. **`mrcr.py` — thin MRCR adapter.** Loads the dataset and turns it into a deterministically-selected, length-ordered request set.

Because the raw table is the source of truth, reports can be re-sliced with different bin edges and **no server** via `rebin.py`, and plotted with `plot.py acceptance`.

Correctness is intentionally not graded — MRCR is used only for its long prompts.

### Deterministic superset selection

Records are stratified into MRCR's native power-of-2 token bins and, within each bin, ranked by a stable content hash (`sha256(seed + prompt)`); the lowest-ranked `--samples-per-bin` per bin form the candidate set. Bin assignment uses `n_chars / 4.9` (MRCR carries no token count; the ratio is 4.9 ± 0.1 across the whole dataset, validated offline against o200k) — zero runtime cost, no `tiktoken` dependency. The candidate set is independent of `max_model_len`; the only context-dependent step is the render fit-test, which is monotonic, so `Kept(ctx1) ⊆ Kept(ctx2)` for `ctx1 ≤ ctx2`. Batches run smallest-first and stop once a whole bin renders oversized.

### CLI

```bash
# Server must expose the render endpoint and per-request detailed metrics:
VLLM_ENABLE_SCALE_OUT_ENDPOINTS=1 vllm serve <model> \
    --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed \
    --speculative-config '{"model":"<draft>","num_speculative_tokens":N}'

python evaluate.py --target http://localhost:8000/v1 long-context --samples-per-bin 20

# Re-slice results offline with different bins (no server):
python rebin.py --table <out>/raw_table --context-bin-edges 0,8192,32768,131072

# Plot the acceptance figure offline (no server):
python plot.py acceptance --table <out>/raw_table --output <out>/acceptance.png
```

New flags (long-context only): `--samples-per-bin`, `--selection-seed`, `--position-bin-size`. `throughput`/`sweep` are unchanged and don't import the long-context deps.

### Visualization

`plot.py` gains an **`acceptance`** subcommand that renders the recorded table into one figure — another pure slicing of the same source of truth as the CSVs, so it needs no server:

![Long-context acceptance plot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reed-meyerson/speculators/pr-assets/acceptance_example.png)

Three panels share one context-length x-axis (example: Qwen3-8B + a DFlash speculator, 7 speculative tokens, MRCR 2-needle):

- **Mean accept len** (line) — mean committed tokens per verify step in each context bin; the headline trend.
- **Tokens generated** (bars) — committed tokens per bin, i.e. how much data backs each column. Deliberately *decoupled* from acceptance (a step-count bar would inflate low-acceptance bins), so it reads cleanly as sample size.
- **Acceptance-length distribution** (heatmap) — within each context bin, the share of verify **steps** that committed exactly *k* tokens (each column sums to ~100%). The integer in a cell is just the precise readout of its color.

The x-axis is the *running* context length at each verify step (prompt length + everything committed so far), not per-request — so it stays meaningful even when generation is long relative to the bin width. Bins default to ~2 log2 bins per octave and can be overridden with `--context-bin-edges`.

Reading the example: acceptance degrades monotonically as context grows — mean length falls 2.73 → 1.68 tokens/step from ~4k to ~26k, and the share of single-token steps climbs 28% → 52%.

### Dependencies

Long-context mode adds `pandas`, `pyarrow`, `huggingface_hub` (dataset loading + Parquet table); requests go straight to the target server's HTTP API, so there's no separate eval harness. Plotting reuses the existing `matplotlib`/`numpy` deps — nothing new.

### Validation

Ran end-to-end against Qwen3-8B + a DFlash speculator at `--max-model-len 40960`: deterministic bounded selection with the bin early-stop firing, a Parquet table written (one part file per bin), both acceptance reports produced, detailed per-step metrics flowing through, `rebin.py` reproducing the reports offline with different bin edges, and `plot.py acceptance` rendering the figure above from the recorded table. Recording is small — a full MRCR run is single-digit MB (the raw prompts are *not* stored, only a reference; the per-step arrays are bounded by the generation cap, not the context length).

### Note

Supersedes #1064 — this replaces the earlier Inspect-AI-based MRCR mode with the recorded-table architecture. Opening fresh rather than force-pushing that branch so the two approaches can be compared. Draft while I gather more validation.

The example image is hosted on the fork's `pr-assets` branch (kept out of this PR's diff), since `gh` can't upload to GitHub's attachment CDN directly.

---

Reusability: `throughput`/`sweep` could later adopt `request_runner` + `acceptance_report` to get the same per-request table and reporting (out of scope here).

title: feat(dflash): support multimodal (VL) training with plain-rope drafts
body:
## Purpose

Enable DFlash drafts to train against multimodal (VL) such as Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3-VL.

The data pipeline is already algorithm-agnostic and multimodal-capable: image rows ride the Chat Completions path (vLLM is served with `--allowed-local-media-path` and runs the full VLM forward), and the captured verifier hidden states already encode the image content - the draft itself never sees pixels. The training forward uses plain 1D position ids for every speculator.

The one gap was draft config construction: `create_transformer_layer_config` inherited `mrope_section` from the verifier's `text_config` into the draft config (the EAGLE-3 mechanism), while

- the training forward is plain 1D, and
- vLLM's DFlash serving path rejects MRoPE draft configs outright.

This PR strips `mrope_section` (and, via the existing guard, the coupled `partial_rotary_factor`) from the draft config for DFlash speculators (`PLAIN_ROPE_DRAFT_SPECULATORS`). The draft's rope is only an internal distance metric for its own attention - the verifier's (3, N) MRoPE positions carry no signal for the draft - so plain rope keeps train/serve consistent for free. This also matches the official `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash` checkpoint, whose draft config ships `rope_scaling: null`.

Also adds:

- an end-to-end online example, `examples/train/dflash_qwen3_5_4b_sharegpt4v_online_5k.sh`, mirroring the official Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash draft geometry (block size 16, 5 draft layers, aux target layers [1, 8, 15, 22, 29], vocab 248320);
- a "Multimodal (VL) Verifiers" section in `docs/user_guide/algorithms/dflash.md`.

The same plain-rope design was validated end-to-end in the SpecForge implementation, see [sgl-project/SpecForge#730](https://github.com/sgl-project/SpecForge/pull/730) for details.

## Tests

Unit tests for the new rope-config behavior: `dflash` strips `mrope_section` on both the transformers>=5 `rope_parameters` path and the pre-5 `rope_scaling` path (the coupled `partial_rotary_factor` is dropped by the existing guard, `rope_theta` preserved), while `eagle3` keeps `mrope_section` when `speculator_type` is passed.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/train/test_rope_config.py tests/unit/train/test_draft_config_init.py tests/unit/train/config -q
# 129 passed
```

E2E: a new multimodal dflash case in `tests/e2e/smoke/test_offline_training.py` (Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct + `sharegpt4v_coco`) covers render -> offline hidden-state extraction with images -> training -> vLLM inference validation of the trained checkpoint; a leaked `mrope_section` would surface at the vLLM engine step. The multimodal online path is already covered by the existing MM case in `test_online_training.py`.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/e2e/smoke/test_offline_training.py --collect-only -q
# 6 tests collected
bash -n examples/train/dflash_qwen3_5_4b_sharegpt4v_online_5k.sh
# no syntax errors

title: fix(loading): resolve Mamba-backbone verifier final-norm key
body:
**Purpose.** DFlash/DFlash2/DSpark carry a frozen `verifier_norm` and load the verifier's final
norm as `model.norm.weight`. HF Mamba-backbone verifiers (NemotronH — Nano/Super/Ultra —,
Mamba/Mamba2, FalconMamba) name it `backbone.norm_f.weight`, which the alias map doesn't resolve. On
a real checkpoint the bare `norm.weight` alias then suffix-matches a per-layer
`backbone.layers.N.norm.weight` and loads it as the final norm — silently, no warning (the quieter
secondary case, a checkpoint with only `backbone.norm_f.weight`, falls back to identity `weight=1.0`).
Either mis-scales the reconstructed targets (cf. #1090). Measured on Nemotron-3-Nano: the tensor
`main` actually loads reconstructs the verifier's top-1 target correctly only **65.0%** of the time,
vs a **99.6%** sanity gate for the correct norm. Fixes #1164.

**Fix.** Add `backbone.norm_f.weight` to `_WEIGHT_ALIASES["model.norm.weight"]`, ordered before the
bare `norm.weight` suffix so the specific final-norm key wins over per-layer norms. Follows the
per-architecture alias pattern of #1158 (embedding), #719, #989. Standard verifiers are byte-unchanged.

**Tests.** Resolver unit tests: final norm resolves; not confused with per-layer norms; standard
`model.norm.weight` unaffected. `ruff` clean; `pytest tests/unit/utils/test_loading.py` green.

title: Check DFlash2 layers by capability, not by exact type
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #1137.

`DFlashDraftModel._make_decoder_layer` is documented as the override point for DFlash-family variants, but `DFlash2SpeculatorModel.__init__` then asserts every layer is exactly `Qwen3DFlash2DecoderLayer`, so that override raises. The assertion is also stronger than the next line needs — it only requires a layer able to reset its convolutions — and as an `assert` it is stripped under `python -O`.

The `hasattr` check keeps the same protection, names the offending class, and lets the documented override work.

## Tests

```python
import torch

class Resettable(torch.nn.Module):
    def reset_convolutions(self): ...

class NotResettable(torch.nn.Module):
    pass

title: fix(loading): resolve Mamba-backbone verifier embedding key
body:
Fixes #1156.

## Problem
HF-format Mamba-backbone verifiers name the input embedding `backbone.embeddings.weight` (NemotronH — verified on the published Nano/Super/Ultra checkpoints; Mamba/Mamba2/FalconMamba per their transformers `modeling_*.py`). None of the current `embed_tokens.weight` candidates is a suffix of that key, so `_resolve_key` returns `None` and `SpeculatorModelBase._load_verifier_weights` raises `KeyError: 'embed_tokens.weight'`. Every algorithm loads the verifier embedding through that base method (eagle3/peagle, dflash/dflash2/dspark, mtp), so all are affected; reproduced end-to-end with eagle3 and dflash.

## Fix
Add `backbone.embeddings.weight` to `_WEIGHT_ALIASES["embed_tokens.weight"]`, following the per-architecture alias pattern of #989, #719, #1038. Kept specific (not a bare `embeddings.weight`) so the resolver's `endswith` scan can't misresolve unrelated tensors such as `position_embeddings.weight`. Standard `model.embed_tokens.weight` verifiers (llama/qwen/gemma, and llama-style hybrids Bamba/Jamba/Zamba2) are byte-unchanged — they match the primary candidate before the alias is consulted. Scope: HF/transformers-format checkpoints (original `mamba_ssm` exports use singular `backbone.embedding.weight`, out of scope).

## Tests
Adds resolver unit tests: the backbone key resolves, standard verifiers are unaffected, and boundary decoys (`position_embeddings.weight`/`word_embeddings.weight`) don't misresolve. `make quality` and `pytest tests/unit/utils/test_loading.py` pass locally.

Note: the open pretraining RFC (#1127) also reads the verifier embedding for the DFlash family, so it would hit the same gap once it lands.

title: feat(hs_connectors): add HTTP backend for hidden-states transfer
body:
## Motivation

In the online hidden-states generation pipeline (`--on-missing generate`), the vLLMconnector writes each freshly extracted hidden-states tensor to `shared_storage_path`. Pointing that at a shared network filesystem (e.g. cephfs) makes every write a cross-host op that contends on the MDS; under saturation, batches of writes stall together with 1–3 s tail latency, which punches through the trainer's prefetch buffer and produces tail training steps.

## What this adds

A new `http` hidden-states backend (`--hidden-states-backend http`):

 - **vLLM side (connector unchanged)**: writes to a local fast disk on its own node — no MDS, no cross-host write bursts.
 - **Trainer side**: `HttpTransfer` fetches the file over plain HTTP from `scripts/serve_hs.py`, a tiny static file server running next to vLLM. It blocks on the same `.lock` flock protocol as the `file` backend, so a fetch never sees a half-written file. After use, `DELETE` removes the data file and its lock.

No shared filesystem is required between vLLM and the trainer, and the whole path depends only on the Python standard library (`http.server` + `flock`).

### Crash safety

- **Trainer crash**: a background TTL sweeper in `serve_hs.py` deletes stale `.safetensors` files (and their `.lock` companions) older than `--ttl` seconds (default 600 s, swept every `--ttl-interval` = 60 s). Orphaned files on the vLLM node's local disk are reclaimed automatically, so a crashed trainer can only leak bounded local disk usage.
- **Races**: a GET that loses a race with a concurrent DELETE (or the TTL sweeper) after its lock-wait answers 404, which `HttpTransfer` maps to `None` so the trainer can re-request.

## Performance

Two independent latency sources:

1. **Poll wakeup granularity** (~51 ms/step): the trainer-side `wait_for_lock()` polls the connector's flock once per `poll_interval`, waking on average half a period late. With the 100 ms default this added ~50 ms to every generated-sample fetch. Fixed for the `file` backend by commit 2 (100 ms → 20 ms default).
2. **Shared-filesystem MDS saturation bursts** (~29–57 ms/step): batches of concurrent connector writes to cephfs stall together with 1–3 s tail latency, punching through the trainer's prefetch buffer and producing tail steps. Eliminated by the `http` backend: vLLM writes to local disk on its own node, the trainer fetches over HTTP.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/hs_connectors/test_http_roundtrip.py` (commit 3): full producer/consumer loop without any vLLM dependency — flock write protocol, lock-blocking semantics, 404-to-None mapping. 3 tests, all passing; upstream hs_connectors and train unit suites pass unchanged (28 + 292 passed).

## Usage

```bash

# on each vLLM node
python scripts/serve_hs.py --root /data/local_hs --port 9010

# trainer
--hidden-states-backend http \
--hidden-states-path  /data/local_hs \
--hs-http-base        http://<vllm-node>:9010

title: feat(plugins): dynamic hidden-states layer swap for extract_hidden_states
body:
## Summary

Adds a self-contained vLLM **plugin** (`vllm_plugins/dynamic_hidden_states`) that
lets you swap **which** target-model hidden layers are captured during
speculator training-data generation (`method="extract_hidden_states"`) **at
runtime over HTTP**, without restarting the engine. Only the *set* of layer
indices changes; the *count* is fixed at launch (proposer buffers, dummy-proposer
KV-cache shape and on-disk safetensors layout depend on it), so count changes are
rejected (fail closed).

This is opt-in and touches no vLLM core files — it wires in entirely through
public plugin entry points and `--worker-extension-cls`.

## How it works

- **`graph_patch.install`** (`vllm.general_plugins`) — a *pre-compile*
  monkeypatch of `EagleModelMixin._maybe_add_hidden_state` /
  `_set_aux_hidden_state_layers`. The stock capture uses a Python membership test
  (`if layer_idx in self.aux_hidden_state_layers`) that `torch.compile`
  constant-folds into the compiled forward, freezing the selection — so a naive
  attribute swap is a silent no-op unless the engine runs `--enforce-eager`.
  Instead we keep `N` fixed accumulator buffers and fold every candidate layer's
  residual into them weighted by a one-hot **selection mask held in a registered
  buffer**. The graph becomes selection-agnostic, so a swap is an in-place
  `mask.copy_(...)` — same storage address, read live by both the compiled graph
  and captured CUDA graphs. **No recompile, no `--enforce-eager`.** Memory stays
  O(N); the cost is a small multiply-add over every candidate layer's residual
  (~0.006% of forward FLOPs).
- **`AuxLayerWorkerExtension`** (`--worker-extension-cls`) — engine-side RPC
  (`get`/`set_aux_hidden_state_layers_rpc`) callable through `collective_rpc`.
- **`AuxLayerEndpoint`** (`vllm.endpoint_plugins`) — registers
  `GET`/`POST /aux_hidden_state_layers` on the OpenAI-compatible server.

## Testing

Verified on Qwen3-8B (1×H100) under the **default** `torch.compile` +
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs (no `--enforce-eager`):

- Swapping only the first captured layer (2→6) changes exactly column 0
  (`max|Δ|=21.125`) while columns for unchanged layers 18/34 stay
  **bit-identical** (`Δ=0`).
- The compiled masked path reproduces the eager baked path's values **exactly**.
- **No recompilation** is triggered by a swap.
- Count-mismatch and empty-layer requests are rejected with `400`.

An end-to-end integration script is included at
`vllm_plugins/tests/test_swap_e2e.py` (run manually against a live server; see
its docstring and `vllm_plugins/README.md`).

## Scope / limitations

- Covers models that capture through `EagleModelMixin._maybe_add_hidden_state`
  (Qwen2/Qwen3, Llama, generic dense/MoE). Models that inline the membership test
  in their own forward (e.g. `deepseek_v2`, `qwen3_next`) are **not** covered by
  the compile patch and still need `--enforce-eager` for a live swap.
- The hidden-states connector's safetensors carry no layer-set metadata, so a
  controller that swaps mid-run must record its own `{time/req-range → layer set}`
  mapping.

## Notes

Opening as a **draft** for discussion — feedback welcome on whether this belongs
here as a plugin vs. upstreaming the masked-accumulate capture into vLLM core.

title: fix(datagen): store MM messages column as JSON to keep shard schemas …
body:
## Purpose

Multimodal conversations with tool calls don't survive the round-trip from preprocessing to the vLLM hidden-states request. Three failure modes, all hit on real-world multimodal agent-trajectory data (UI-action SFT corpora with tool calls):

1. **Preprocessing crash with `num_proc > 1`**: `build_eagle3_dataset`'s `dataset.map` declares no `features`, so each worker shard infers its own Arrow schema for the structured `messages` column. Shards holding different conversation shapes (optional `tool_calls`, plain-string vs typed-part-list `content`) disagree, and the final concatenation fails:
   `ValueError: The features can't be aligned because the key messages of features {...} has unexpected type`

2. **Tool-call requests rejected by vLLM**: HF chat templates require assistant `tool_calls[].function.arguments` as dicts, but the OpenAI Chat Completions schema vLLM validates against requires a JSON *string* — so requests carrying dict arguments get `400: Input should be a valid string` and those samples are silently dropped. (Reading the prepared dataset in torch format additionally converts numeric argument leaves, e.g. click coordinates, into tensors, failing request serialization outright with `Object of type Tensor is not JSON serializable`.)

3. **Tool definitions dropped from the request**: chat templates render `tools` into the prompt, so preprocessing tokenizes with them — but only `messages` were sent to vLLM. The re-rendered prompt omits the tools block, and `--validate-outputs` rejects every tool-using multimodal sample with `Prompt token IDs mismatch`.

## Description

- `_preprocess_batch` serializes each row's messages with `json.dumps`, so the column is always `Value("string")` — deterministic regardless of sharding, and immune to torch-format tensor conversion.
- The parsed `tools` each conversation was tokenized with are stored alongside, as a JSON-string column for the same reason.
- `build_client_item` (the single consumer, shared by online training and offline datagen) decodes the JSON string, re-encodes dict tool-call arguments as JSON strings for the API (vLLM decodes them back to dicts server-side before rendering its chat template), and forwards `tools` in the request body.
- Datasets prepared before this change hold structured rows and no `tools` column; both are still accepted.

## Tests

- New regression test `test_build_eagle3_dataset_multiproc_heterogeneous_conversations`: mixed string/typed-part conversations (with a heterogeneous `tools` column) through `build_eagle3_dataset` with `num_proc=2`. Verified it reproduces the alignment crash on `main` and passes with this change.
- New unit tests for `build_client_item`: JSON-string multimodal messages are decoded and forwarded, text-only messages are omitted, legacy structured rows keep working, dict tool-call arguments are stringified (string arguments pass through), and `tools` are forwarded only alongside multimodal messages.
- New unit tests for `_chat_extra_body`: re-render flags, Mistral `continue_final_message` special case, tools included when present / omitted when absent.

title: fix(loss): normalize training loss by global (cross-rank) token count
body:
## Purpose

`loss_function` (`src/speculators/models/metrics.py`) normalizes the masked training loss by the **per-rank** supervised-token count:

```python
denominator = loss_mask.sum(dim=1) + _EPS
batch_loss  = torch.sum(elementwise_loss, dim=1) / denominator
return batch_loss.mean()
```

Under DDP/FSDP the per-rank gradients are then **mean-averaged**, so the effective objective is the rank-local mean of ratios

```
(1/R) · Σ_r ( Σ_t loss_r / Σ_t mask_r )
```

rather than the token-weighted objective

```
( Σ_r Σ_t loss ) / ( Σ_r Σ_t mask )
```

These differ whenever the per-rank supervised-token counts are uneven: a token's weight in the update ends up depending on which rank it landed on.

This is not prevented by packing. `_lpt_packed_batch` balances **total** tokens against a budget (and its docstring notes that "slot 0 always takes the largest sample and the highest slot absorbs the small ones", so sample counts stay skewed), while the loss denominator counts **supervised** tokens — the packer never looks at `loss_mask`. Two ranks can hold the same token budget and still differ substantially in how many positions are unmasked: one rank holding a single long sample has one masked prompt, while a rank absorbing many small samples pays that prompt cost many times over.

For reference, DeepSpec computes its backward loss this way (`_build_loss`): each term is `local_numerator / all_reduced_denominator`, and the sum is scaled by `world_size`; the rank-local denominators are used only for reported metrics.

## Fix

When distributed, all-reduce the denominator to the global token count and scale by `world_size`, so the subsequent gradient mean-average reconstructs the token-weighted objective.

- **Gradient-identical when ranks are token-balanced** (single rank, or balanced supervised-token counts) — a no-op for that case, so it does not shift the effective LR of tuned recipes.
- Only changes behavior — correctly — when per-rank supervised-token counts are imbalanced.
- The all-reduce is on the **detached denominator only**; autograd flows through this rank's numerator exactly as before.
- Uses the default process group, matching `fully_shard`'s gradient reduction; correct under sequence parallelism as well, where summing across shards recovers the full sequence's token count.
- Batch is `[1, seq_len]` after collation, so within-rank semantics are unchanged; only the cross-rank normalization changes.
- Cost is one scalar all-reduce per loss term per step; the call is rank-symmetric, like the collectives the trainer already performs.
- Device-agnostic; no new dependencies.

## Fix

title: Count only evaluable positions in the conditional accuracy denominator
body:
## Problem

For eagle3 TTT steps >= 1, the caller slices `loss_mask[:, ttt_step:]` against `prev_correct[:, :-ttt_step]`, so a position can be prev-correct yet not evaluable at this step. `compute_accuracy_single_step` counted the conditional denominator from `prev_correct` alone, before the loss mask applies, while the numerator is loss-masked, so `cond_acc_1/2` are systematically biased low at every assistant-span boundary.

## Fix

The conditional denominator now counts positions that are both prev-correct and inside the loss mask, snapshotted before the in-place `logical_and` update. With `prev_correct=None` and a mask, the denominator is now the masked count for the same reason (previously the unmasked numel). Note for dashboards: logged `cond_acc_*` values step-change across this fix by design.

## Tests

New unit tests pin the masked denominator with and without `prev_correct` (both fail on main); the existing unmasked chain test is unchanged and passes.

title: Seed resumed LR schedulers with the global step, not the epoch index
body:
## Problem

On resume, `setup_optimizer` passes `last_epoch = checkpointer.previous_epoch` (an epoch index) to `get_linear/cosine_schedule_with_warmup`, but these schedulers step once per optimizer step. Whenever `scheduler_state_dict.pt` is missing (e.g. the original run used `scheduler_type="none"`, or an older checkpoint), the resumed schedule sits at step `previous_epoch` of warmup: near-zero LR, then a full re-warmup and re-decay on an already-trained model. Constructing a scheduler with `last_epoch >= 0` can also crash outright with `KeyError: initial_lr` when the loaded optimizer state predates any scheduler.

## Fix

The resume seed is now `self.global_step - 1` (the constructor's initial step advances it by one, matching a fresh scheduler stepped `global_step` times), `initial_lr` is backfilled into param groups that lack it, and a warning is logged when `scheduler_state_dict.pt` is absent, including the caveat that checkpoints without `training_state.json` read `global_step` as 0 and restart warmup.

## Tests

Unit tests assert the resumed scheduler's `last_epoch` and LR exactly match a fresh scheduler advanced by the same number of optimizer steps, and that fresh runs still start at -1. The resume test fails on main (KeyError: initial_lr, and wrong LR position with state loaded).

title: Save and load optimizer state at full precision in checkpoints
body:
## Problem

Checkpointing converts the entire optimizer state dict to bf16 (the default `float_dtype`), including the AdamW `exp_avg`/`exp_avg_sq` moments and the float `step` counters. bf16 has an 8-bit mantissa: any step count above 256 rounds (10000 rounds to a multiple of 64), and the second moments lose their low bits, so resumed runs use wrong bias correction and quantized moments, visibly deviating from an uninterrupted run. Both `SingleGPUCheckpointer` and `DistributedCheckpointer` are affected, and the load paths re-applied the same cast (to the model dtype), so bf16 models were re-quantized even when the file was fine.

## Fix

Optimizer state is saved and loaded without any dtype conversion. `Optimizer.load_state_dict` already aligns per-param float state with the param dtype and leaves `step` untouched; the distributed loader's step-to-float32 repair loop is kept for legacy bf16-saved checkpoints. Model weights still save as bf16 as before.

Note on scope: this changes what new checkpoints contain (optimizer state roughly doubles in size, fp32 instead of bf16) while remaining able to load old bf16-saved files. Flagging it here since it touches the checkpoint save/load path; happy to adjust if you prefer an opt-in flag.

## Tests

A round-trip unit test in `test_checkpoint.py` steps AdamW past step 10000, saves, reloads through the checkpointer, and asserts the step counters and moments are bit-exact fp32. Fails on main.

title: [RFC][Data] Collapse the pipeline around one on-policy contract
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is an intentionally broad proof of concept for design discussion, not a merge-ready change. It depends on [#794](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/pull/794), which introduces the target-model render boundary that makes this simplification possible. If the design is accepted, the implementation will be rebuilt from a fresh branch as small reviewable PRs.

> [!WARNING]
> #794's head branch lives in a fork, so GitHub cannot use it as the base of a second PR in this repository. This draft therefore targets `main`, and its “Files changed” view includes #794. The refactor-only delta starts after `071f37c` and can be reviewed in this [focused comparison](https://github.com/WindChimeRan/speculators/compare/feat/render-boundary-loss-mask...codex/rfc-on-policy-data-pipeline).

![Proposed on-policy data pipeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WindChimeRan/speculators/881b5d298feed3ac9eac8b0bca9fc19ecfb10b95/docs/assets/on-policy-data-pipeline-rfc.svg)

## Problem

Speculator training data must be on-policy, but the current preparation pipeline mixes several responsibilities:

- loading raw source presets
- loading a local Hugging Face processor
- applying chat templates and tokenization locally
- rendering conversations through the serving endpoint
- accepting pre-tokenized rows
- normalizing conversations and tools
- retaining processor-specific message state
- producing visualization and review-only text

These overlapping paths duplicate logic and make the data contract difficult to explain. More importantly, accepting a raw source preset directly in preparation makes it possible to train on that dataset's assistant responses even though they were not generated by the target model.

The proposed invariant is:

> Every supervised token was generated by the target model. Rendering may encode an on-policy conversation, but it must never turn a source dataset's assistant response into a training target.

## Proposed pipeline

There are three supported inputs:

1. **Raw prompt preset**
   - Accepted by target response regeneration.
   - Existing assistant turns are discarded.
   - The target endpoint generates replacement responses and returns their token IDs.

2. **User-provided on-policy conversation**
   - Accepted by preparation through a local JSON/JSONL file or an explicit `hf:` dataset.
   - The target endpoint's render API applies the serving chat template and identifies assistant boundaries.
   - Rendering does not generate, replace, or validate response provenance; the user is responsible for providing on-policy conversations.

3. **Already prepared data**
   - Contains `input_ids` and `loss_mask`.
   - Skips endpoint rendering and is validated directly.

All paths converge on one internal contract:

```python
class PreparedSample(TypedDict):
    input_ids: list[int]
    loss_mask: list[int]
    messages: NotRequired[list[dict]]
```

One finalizer then validates mask shape and values, truncates, filters, and tensorizes the samples.

## Settled design choices in this prototype

### PreparedSample is the single internal boundary

Response regeneration, rendered conversations, and prepared input all produce the same representation before dataset construction. Optional `messages` exist only for downstream requests that genuinely require multimodal content.

### Conversation failures are reported and skipped

A malformed or unrenderable conversation does not abort an entire dataset. Prepared rows still fail validation for structural errors such as mismatched lengths or non-binary masks.

### Tool results are unsupervised environment observations

Source assistant tool calls are discarded and regenerated by the target model. Cached tool results may be paired with a compatible regenerated call so generation can continue, but tool results are never included in the supervised completion mask. Preparation only renders complete on-policy tool conversations and never executes tools.

### Multimodal remains a placeholder

The generic `messages` field, content adaptation, and downstream multimodal routing remain in the contract. The direct ShareGPT4V/COCO preset path is removed because it does not currently have a supported on-policy regeneration flow. A future focused PR can build that flow without reintroducing source assistant responses as targets.

### Per-assistant-turn fan-out is intentional

Some chat templates rewrite earlier history and therefore do not have a stable append-only boundary. In that case, preparation emits one sample per assistant turn so each target span has a defensible render boundary.

## What the proof of concept removes

- `prepare_data.py --model` and `--trust-remote-code`
- local `AutoProcessor` loading and tokenizer setup during preparation
- processor objects from the preparation API
- duplicate conversation normalization and tool-schema parsing
- review-only detokenized `text` in regeneration output
- local preprocessing visualization and detokenization machinery
- `logging_utils.py` and `torch_utils.py`
- direct raw-preset preparation and its off-policy examples/tests
- the unsupported direct ShareGPT4V/COCO preset path

Relative to #794, the refactor is **610 additions / 1,330 deletions**, a net reduction of **720 lines**, including tests and documentation.

## User-facing migration

- Raw presets such as `sharegpt`, `gsm8k`, and `hermes-fc` must go through response regeneration first.
- User-provided natural-language data must already be on-policy and requires `--render-endpoint`.
- Prepared `input_ids` / `loss_mask` data requires no endpoint.
- Training still loads the verifier tokenizer when it needs model metadata such as `mask_token_id`; only data preparation stops loading a local model processor.



## RFC question for maintainers

If this end state is directionally correct, how should the fresh implementation be divided into reviewable PRs?

One possible sequence is:

1. establish the shared `PreparedSample` contract and finalizer on top of #794
2. share conversation normalization and strict tool parsing
3. make preparation accept only on-policy conversations or prepared rows
4. integrate response regeneration, including cached tool observations
5. remove obsolete processor, visualization, logging, and compatibility paths; migrate docs and examples
6. add true on-policy multimodal source regeneration in a later focused PR
7. integrate into `speculator-cli`

This PR contains (2-5)

The sequence is illustrative; maintainer feedback on dependencies and review boundaries is the purpose of this RFC.

title: Add Ulysses SP for Training
body:
## Purpose

** updated description to help with review, got claude to write a lot of it but I reviewed this

Add ulysses sequence parallelism(SP) for speculator training. Long-context training is memory-bound by activations that scale with sequence length — Ulysses SP shards the packed sequence across multiple GPUs using all-to-all communication, reducing per-GPU activation memory proportionally.

Enabled with `--sp-size <N>` (default 1, off). Supported for Eagle3, PEagle, DFlash, and DSpark. Works with both DDP and FSDP (`--fsdp-shard`).

This version uses scoped DDP/FSDP + explicit gradient hooks, which cleanly separates the sum-across-SP and average-across-DP reduction semantics.

## Design

SP groups use contiguous ranks, DP groups use strided ranks. For example, with `world_size=4, sp_size=2`:

```
SP groups: {0,1}, {2,3}    (process same batch, different seq chunks)
DP groups: {0,2}, {1,3}    (process different batches, same seq position)
```

A 2D `DeviceMesh("dp", "sp")` is created when `sp_size > 1` so FSDP can scope its sharding to the DP sub-mesh only. 

DDP/FSDP all-reduce uses averaging, but SP partial gradients must be summed (each rank sees a fraction of the sequence, not a fraction of the batch). These are different operations on different axes:

- `register_sp_gradient_hooks` uses `post_accumulate_grad_hook` to SUM gradients across the SP group (handles `DTensor` from FSDP transparently)
- DDP/FSDP is scoped to the DP group, where averaging is correct

The loss function (`loss_function` in `metrics.py`) all-reduces the numerator and denominator across the SP group in the forward pass (detached from autograd) so every SP rank computes the same scalar loss. The gradient hooks handle the backward side.

### Per-model SP strategy

Models differ in how they handle the sequence dimension, captured by the `_sp_splits_batch` ClassVar:

| Model | `_sp_splits_batch` | Strategy |
|-------|-------------------|----------|
| **Eagle3** | `True` (default) | Trainer splits batch; model sees local seq chunk for all tensors except `document_ids` (kept full for global position info) |
| **DFlash** | `False` | Handles SP internally — builds attention mask at full dims on rank 0, broadcasts anchors, then partitions anchors per SP rank. Uses a custom `dflash_flex_attention` attention impl that handles the context+noise layout. |
| **DSpark** | `False` (inherits DFlash) | Inherits DFlash's SP slicing. Derives `num_blocks` from `anchored_block_indices` shape instead of `max_anchors` arg (correct under SP partitioning). |
| **PEagle** | `False` | COD samples are generated on rank 0 and broadcast to SP group. Samples are padded for divisibility and partitioned, with a `pad_mask` to zero out padded positions in the loss. |

### Attention all-to-all

The Ulysses all-to-all is integrated into `flex_attention_forward`:

1. Q/K/V arrive in sequence-parallel layout: `(B, H, S_local, D)`
2. `ulysses_scatter` transposes to head-parallel layout: `(B, H/sp, S_full, D)` — each rank gets a subset of heads but the full sequence
3. `flex_attention` runs with the full sequence visible per head (standard causal/block mask)
4. `ulysses_gather` transposes back: `(B, H, S_local, D)`

KV heads are replicated when `num_kv_heads < sp_size` (via `maybe_replicate_kv_heads`) to ensure every SP rank gets at least one KV head after the scatter.

### Batch splitting

`split_batch_for_sp` in the trainer splits the batch along the sequence dimension before each forward pass (for models with `_sp_splits_batch=True`). Keys in `_SPLIT_KEYS` (hidden_states, verifier_last_hidden_states, input_ids, loss_mask, position_ids) are chunked; keys in `_KEEP_FULL_KEYS` (document_ids) are kept full. A `full_seq_len` sentinel is injected for downstream code that needs the global length.

## Usage

```bash
# 8 GPUs, sp_size=2: sequences split across pairs of GPUs
torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 scripts/train.py \
  --sp-size 2 \
  --fsdp-shard \
  --draft-attn-impl simple_flex_attention \
  --total-seq-len 65536 \
  ...
```

Constraints:
- `--total-seq-len` must be divisible by `--sp-size`
- `world_size` must be divisible by `--sp-size`
- `--draft-attn-impl` must be `simple_flex_attention` (eager/sdpa don't go through the SP-aware attention path)
- `--max-anchors` must be divisible by `--sp-size` (DFlash/DSpark only)

## Tests

- 15 unit tests for `split_batch_for_sp` and `maybe_replicate_kv_heads`
- 9 unit tests for `normalize_counted_metrics`
- 5 multi-GPU tests: SP group initialization (sp_size=1 and sp_size=2), all-to-all round-trip correctness, all-to-all backward gradient correctness, SP gradient hook all-reduce
- E2E verified on all four architectures (Eagle3, DFlash, DSpark, PEagle) with memory reduction confirmed

title: fix(dspark): loss mask off-by-one
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Affects `sample_from_anchor=True`, DSpark's default. DFlash defaults to False and is unchanged.


A draft slot was gated by the loss mask at its own position instead of at the token it predicts. A hidden state at position *i* yields the distribution over token *i+1*, so the mask has to be read one position ahead.

Assistant turn at positions 8-39, `block_size=4`, anchor `a=37`:

```
slot j             0    1    2    3
position a+j      37   38   39   40
predicts token    38   39   40   41
is it content?   yes  yes   no   no     <- turn ends at 39

before           [1,   1,   1,   0]     <- loss_mask[a+j]
after            [1,   1,   0,   0]     <- loss_mask[a+j+1]
                            ^ trained on the turn separator
```

```python
# before
aligned_loss_mask = loss_mask.clone()[:, anchored_block_indices]

# after
mask_indices = (
    anchored_block_indices + 1
    if self.config.sample_from_anchor
    else anchored_block_indices
)
aligned_loss_mask = loss_mask.clone()[:, mask_indices]
```

The two indices only disagree where the mask changes, so this is confined to turn boundaries — 0.47% of supervised slots at 200-token turns, 5.7% at 20-token turns, always over-supervision.


## Tests

One test: every slot the model marks trainable must be predicting a supervised token. Red with the fix reverted, green with it — the failure is the bug stated directly, `loss_mask` sampled at each trained slot's predicted token, which should be all ones.

```

E   + where ... = tensor([1., 1., 1., ..., 1., 1., 0.]).all
```

```

pytest tests/unit/models -q                                                 137 passed

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

## Warning!! This PR is from static code analysis, not tested end2end on kimi2.5!
## Purpose

On-policy regeneration appends each reply to the running prefix as `content` alone, dropping the `reasoning` the server just parsed out. Chat templates read that field to decide whether a turn's reasoning is re-rendered into the next prompt, so every turn after the first was conditioned on a prefix serving would not produce.

Take a two-step tool call on Kimi K2.5. The target reasons, calls `get_weather`, and the second request has to re-render that call as history:

```jsonc
// what regen sends back for turn 2
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", ...}]}
```

```text
// before -- the reasoning behind the call is gone
<|im_assistant|>assistant<|im_middle|><think></think><|tool_calls_section_begin|>...

// after -- it survives, as it does when serving
<|im_assistant|>assistant<|im_middle|><think>Need the weather tool for Tokyo.</think><|tool_calls_section_begin|>...
```

Kimi K2.5 preserves reasoning for exactly the in-flight tool loop and reads it only from `reasoning_content` -- no fallback. Qwen3 hid the bug because its template splits `<think>` back out of `content` when the field is missing, so the same defect is invisible there and silent here.

This forwards the field. It reads either response spelling (current vLLM answers with `reasoning`, older builds used `reasoning_content`) and sends the older one, which current vLLM normalizes and older builds pass through untouched. Without `--reasoning-parser` there is no field on the response, nothing is carried, and behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

One test, on the tool-call path -- the branch where a real template actually loses the data.

Red without the source change, green with it:

```
E  assert {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [...]}
        == {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [...],
            "reasoning_content": "Need the weather tool."}
```

pytest tests/unit/scripts/test_response_regeneration.py -q
44 passed
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy --check-untyped-defs` (174 files) all pass.

title: Add gradient accumulation for training (single-GPU/DDP/FSDP2)
body:
## Summary

Adds a `--gradient-accumulation-steps` / `TrainerConfig.gradient_accumulation_steps` knob (default `1`) that accumulates gradients over N microbatches before each optimizer step, growing the effective batch size (`per-step batch × N`) without extra per-microbatch memory. Matches the convention used by peer speculative-decoding frameworks (DeepSpec, TorchSpec, SpecForge): loss scaled by `1/N`, optimizer + LR scheduler stepped once per accumulation window, counting in optimizer (macro) steps.

## Behavior

- **Macro-step counting**: `global_step`, `--log-freq`, `--checkpoint-freq` (when `< 1`), and the LR scheduler total all advance once per accumulation window (an accum=N run does `1/N` the scheduler steps per epoch).
- **Drop remainder**: trailing microbatches that don't fill a full window are dropped each epoch. `_optimizer_steps_per_epoch` is the single source of truth for this policy (used by the scheduler math, the `__init__` guard, and the loop boundary).
- **`_maybe_no_sync`**: on DDP, skips the gradient all-reduce on non-boundary microbatches and syncs the accumulated gradient on the boundary. Single-GPU (raw module) and FSDP2 (`fully_shard`, DTensor params) fall back to a no-op context and stay correct because gradients accumulate additively into `.grad`.
- **Guardrail**: `Trainer` raises early if N exceeds the batches-per-epoch (which would otherwise run zero optimizer steps).
- **`accum=1` is behavior-identical** to the previous one-step-per-batch loop (regression-safe).

## Verification

Numerically confirmed equivalent to the mean of per-microbatch gradients (accumulated grad vs. reference) on real hardware:

| Path | Launch | cadence (accum=1 / 4) | max abs grad diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-GPU | `python` | 13 / 3 | 3.7e-9 |
| DDP | `torchrun` ×8 | 13 / 3 | 9.3e-9 |
| FSDP2 (`fully_shard`) | `torchrun` ×4 | 13 / 3 | 2.3e-9 |

All three exercise the real `Trainer.train_epoch → _accumulate_and_step → _maybe_no_sync` path. DDP/FSDP2 use different data per rank, so cross-rank averaging composes with accumulation.

Unit tests added: scheduler-step math (accum, remainder, accum=1 regression), numerical grad-equivalence on a toy model, `_maybe_no_sync` behavior (single-process DDP), the accum-too-large guard, and CLI parsing/rejection.

## Test plan

title: feat: add bounded asynchronous hidden-state fan-out
body:
## Purpose

Resolves #810.

Add opt-in bounded asynchronous hidden-state fan-out for independent consumers:

- coalesce identical producer misses and atomically publish one packed artifact;
- maintain an independent sliding window and committed cursor for each consumer;
- retain artifacts only while they belong to a live window or active lease;
- prioritize demand while filling bounded lookahead asynchronously;
- support heterogeneous consumer rates without a shared progress barrier;
- validate 1P1C/1P3C topology, request multiplicity, failure accounting, and common
  steady-state windows in a reproducible benchmark harness;
- record role-aware NVML utilization and memory without initializing CUDA in the
  monitor; and
- reduce DFlash consumer overhead with fused AdamW/integrated clipping and an optional,
  version-pinned Liger fused linear cross-entropy backend.

All new training behavior is opt-in. Existing online/offline data paths and optimizer
defaults remain unchanged. The first shared-artifact backend requires POSIX `flock`,
same-filesystem atomic rename, and directory `fsync`; it does not claim arbitrary NFS
or GPU-direct support.

### Scope and related Mooncake work

This PR does **not** add a Mooncake payload backend. Its shared-artifact cache stores
safetensors on a shared POSIX filesystem, and all 1P3C throughput, memory, and NVML
results below measure that filesystem implementation.

A related Mooncake-backed bounded asynchronous producer/consumer implementation is
publicly available in
[sgl-project/SpecForge#707](https://github.com/sgl-project/SpecForge/pull/707). It includes
zero-copy transport and fan-out lifetime ownership. That implementation provides useful
related validation for the lifecycle invariants and benchmark design here, but its
Mooncake code is not included in this PR.

Upstream Mooncake work already exists in #605 and #710, with #735 providing the merged
hidden-state transfer abstraction and current file backend. This PR does not claim first
Mooncake support or attempt to duplicate those open changes.

The coordinator in this PR currently carries concrete filesystem paths in its read and
eviction leases. Supporting Mooncake for the shared fan-out payload therefore requires a
follow-up refactor to opaque artifact references and a store protocol; it is not an
already supported configuration or a drop-in adapter today. That follow-up should be
coordinated with #605/#710.

title: train: --init-on-meta for large draft model construction
body:
Adds build_on_meta(): a context manager that builds nn.Module parameters on the meta device (buffers stay real), so a large draft is not replicated in host RAM on every rank during construction. Wired into scripts/train.py via --init-on-meta: non-rank0 ranks build on meta and receive real weights via set_model_state_dict(broadcast_from_rank0=True) in FSDP setup; only rank 0 builds real weights. This is the torchtitan/torchtune large-model init pattern.

Opt-in and off by default. The base `load_verifier_weights` now no-ops on meta params, so the built-in speculators work under it through the shared load path (verified end-to-end for Eagle3 — see Tests). The general contract still holds for any *custom* draft: data-dependent init (weight load, or anything calling `.item()`/`.isnan()` on a param) must be guarded with `param.is_meta`.

  <!-- markdownlint-disable -->

  ## Purpose

  For large draft models, having every rank build the full model in host RAM during construction is wasteful — only rank 0's weights survive (the rest are overwritten by the rank-0 broadcast in FSDP setup). `--init-on-meta` lets non-rank0 ranks construct the draft on the `meta` device (≈0 resident memory); real weights then arrive via the trainer's existing `set_model_state_dict(broadcast_from_rank0=True)`. Pure memory optimization — the resulting weights are identical to a normal build.

  Changes:
  - `build_on_meta()` context manager (`speculators/train/distributed.py`): overrides `register_parameter` so params land on `meta`, buffers stay real, and restores the original on exit.
  - `--init-on-meta` flag (`scripts/train.py`, opt-in): wraps draft construction in `build_on_meta()` on non-rank0 ranks.
  - Base `SpeculatorModel.load_verifier_weights()` early-returns when params are on `meta`. Without this, `from_training_args` crashes calling `.isnan()` on a meta tensor (`Tensor.item()
  cannot be called on meta tensors`). Covers eagle3/dflash/dspark/peagle (which don't override the method); harmless no-op for mtp.

## Tests

  **Unit (CPU, runs in CI)** — `tests/unit/train/test_build_on_meta.py`:
  - params land on `meta` while buffers keep real storage/values;
  - the `register_parameter` monkeypatch is restored on exit (no global leak);
  - a real `Eagle3DraftModel.from_training_args(...)` builds under `build_on_meta` (all params meta / buffers real), exercising the `is_meta` guard so the verifier load no-ops instead of

title: feat(dflash): add Domino causal correction head (projector_type=domino)
body:
## Purpose

Adds the **Domino** causal correction head as a `projector_type` sub-mode of the existing DFlash draft model (closes #664, based on training-side work in PR #685).

Domino (arXiv 2605.29707) extends DFlash's parallel draft backbone with a lightweight GRU + low-rank MLP head (~56M params) that refines base logits using causal state from previous draft tokens — entirely in logit space, without extra forward passes. Architecture verified against the paper and the [SpecForge reference implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/SpecForge/pull/571).

Corresponding PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48241

### Architecture

- `DominoHead` module (`prefix_gru` + `embed_proj`) wired into `DFlashDraftModel`
- Dual-branch training objective: `loss = (1 - λ) * final_loss + λ * base_loss` with linear λ decay schedule
- **Accept-Until-Fail (AUF)** loss truncation (`--auf`, arXiv 2607.01893): zeros the loss support after the first prediction error per block, aligning training with the verifier's prefix-acceptance semantics. Works with both plain DFlash and Domino (for Domino, only the base branch is truncated; the final branch keeps the full mask).
- **Decay-weighted loss normalization** (`--normalize-loss-by-decay`): divides the loss by the sum of decay weights instead of the token count, producing a proper weighted average that stabilizes loss magnitude across different gamma values. Matches SGLang's DFlash loss normalization.

### New CLI flags

| Flag | Section | Default | Description |
|------|---------|---------|-------------|
| `--auf` | DFlash | off | Enable AUF truncation (arXiv 2607.01893) — works with both DFlash and Domino |
| `--normalize-loss-by-decay` | DFlash | off | Normalize loss by sum of decay weights instead of token count |
| `--projector-type` | Domino | `dflash` | `domino` to enable the correction head |
| `--domino-gru-hidden-dim` | Domino | `1024` | GRU hidden dimension |
| `--domino-emb-dim` | Domino | `256` | MLP bottleneck dimension |
| `--domino-pure-draft-prefix-len` | Domino | `1` | Positions using pure base logits before GRU correction |
| `--domino-lambda-start` | Domino | `1.0` | Initial base-loss weight λ |
| `--domino-lambda-decay-ratio` | Domino | `1.0` | Fraction of total steps over which λ decays to 0 |

## Tests

```bash

## Summary

Implements **DFlare** ([arXiv:2606.02091](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02091), Tencent), which extends DFlash block diffusion speculative decoding with three improvements that break the depth-scaling saturation ceiling:

- **Adaptive layer fusion**: Per-draft-layer learnable scalar weights (D×T parameters) over target hidden states with softmax normalization and per-layer RMSNorm, replacing the single FC projection
- **Heterogeneous KV projections**: Separate K/V projection matrices for target context vs draft states in attention layers

DFlash suffers from depth-scaling saturation — adding more draft layers beyond ~3 yields diminishing returns because all layers share a single fused representation. Instead of duplicating the standard flat cross-entropy logic, the `MultiLevelLMHead` acts as an auxiliary module that only computes the centroid classification loss using the `token_ordering` mapping buffer. The unreduced centroid loss is then added to the standard token loss inside `core.py`.

title: fix(train): crash-safe checkpoints — completeness marker gating resume
body:
# fix(train): crash-safe checkpoints — completeness marker gating resume

## Summary

`save_checkpoint()` writes `model.safetensors` / `optimizer_state_dict.pt` /
etc. directly to their final paths, and `_get_previous_epoch()` (which resume
uses to find the latest checkpoint) trusts **any directory whose name parses
as an integer** — nothing distinguishes a fully written checkpoint from one
truncated by a crash mid-save.

Failure mode:

1. `save_checkpoint()` for epoch N is killed mid-`save_pretrained()` (OOM,
   preemption, node failure) — directory `N/` now exists with a truncated
   `model.safetensors`.
2. The job restarts; `_get_previous_epoch()` sees `N`, returns it.
3. `load_model_state_dict()` hits the truncated file: best case safetensors
   throws a parse error and the run is stuck until someone deletes `N/` by
   hand; worst case (`optimizer_state_dict.pt` via `torch.load`) a partial
   read surfaces as a confusing unpickling error.

`training_state.json` does not guard this: resume only reads it to pick
mid-epoch vs end-of-epoch, and a missing/corrupt one silently falls back to
"advance to next epoch" — still loading model/optimizer from the broken dir.

## Fix

SpecForge had the identical bug class; the fix follows the same design as
sgl-project/SpecForge#659: a completeness marker written last, gating resume.

- `BaseCheckpointer.mark_checkpoint_complete(epoch)`: fsync every file in the
  epoch dir, then write a `checkpoint_complete` marker (fsync it and the
  directory). The fsyncs matter: after a hard host crash, files can survive
  at full length with truncated content, so the marker must not claim
  completeness before the data is durable.
- `Trainer` calls it once all files of an epoch are in place (model,
  optimizer, scheduler, `training_state.json`, val metrics — the last writes
  happen in the trainer, which is why the marker call lives there).
- `_get_previous_epoch()` skips integer dirs without the marker, logging a
  warning with explicit instructions (`touch .../checkpoint_complete`) —
  the same warn-and-instruct pattern already used for `interrupted/` dirs.
  This also covers checkpoints from before this change.

## Test plan

`tests/unit/train/test_checkpoint.py` (extends the existing suite, CPU-only):

- a dir with files but no marker is skipped; resume falls back to the newest
  complete checkpoint (the crash scenario);
- `mark_checkpoint_complete` makes a checkpoint visible to a fresh
  checkpointer;
- `maybe_save_checkpoint` end-to-end writes the marker.

Full `tests/unit/train/` suite passes (113 passed; 1 pre-existing failure is
a hub-connectivity issue in `test_setup_model.py`, unrelated).


Also require `checkpoint_best` to resolve to a completed checkpoint, so best-validation state cannot be restored from an incomplete epoch.

title: fix(eagle3): fail conversion on unmatched checkpoint keys instead of saving random weights
body:
## Description

Eagle3 conversion silently persisted randomly initialized weights whenever a checkpoint key did not match the model: `Eagle3Converter._save_converted_checkpoint` logged missing and unexpected `load_state_dict` keys as warnings and saved anyway, so any weight the checkpoint failed to provide remained at its random initialization on disk. This is the failure mode behind #358 and #360, where a lost remap produced a checkpoint that converted cleanly and only surfaced as zero acceptance during evaluation.

This change mirrors the MTP and DFlash converters by raising `ValueError` on unexpected keys and on missing keys, since the detached conversion flow fills no weights after load and every model-owned key must come from the checkpoint; the issue reporter verified that all 48 valid flag combinations load with zero missing and unexpected keys, so valid conversions are unaffected. Unit tests cover a renamed checkpoint key, a missing draft layer weight, and a happy path asserting saved tensors equal the source weights.

Fixes #1114

title: fix(train): resolve per-layer config attrs for heterogeneous verifiers
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #1118.

`speculators train` crashes at config-build time on a **heterogeneous per-layer verifier config** (transformers ≥5.15, e.g. `google/gemma-4-31B-it`). `create_transformer_layer_config` reads `head_dim` / `num_key_value_heads` off the **global** verifier config; on heterogeneous configs transformers raises `AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError`, which subclasses `RuntimeError` (not `AttributeError`), so `getattr(config, "head_dim", None)` does **not** swallow it. Fixing only `head_dim` just moves the crash to `num_key_value_heads`.

These reads only seed the draft's *own* default attention block (this branch is skipped under `--draft-config` / `--from-pretrained`), so there is no ground-truth per-layer value to recover — just a default to pick. When the verifier `is_heterogeneous`, this resolves the affected attributes — driven off `verifier_config.per_layer_attributes`, not a hardcoded list — from the single **modal** (most common) layer. That gives a leaner/faster draft (draft latency is on the spec-decoding critical path) and matches the published `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.dflash` draft geometry (`head_dim=256`, `num_key_value_heads=16`). A scoped `num_attention_heads % num_key_value_heads == 0` check guards a future config that also varies query-head count. Homogeneous configs are unchanged.

Only `train/cli.py` is affected — the other `head_dim` reads (`models/dflash`, `models/eagle3`, `convert/eagle`) operate on the drafter's own homogeneous config or a plain dict.

## Tests

Added unit tests in `tests/unit/train/test_draft_config_init.py` with a fake heterogeneous config: modal resolution, a no-global-read guarantee, and the divisibility invariant.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/train/test_draft_config_init.py -q

$ make quality
ruff check / ruff format / mdformat / mypy / sync_provenance  -> all pass

title: feat(eval): agentic-coding-trajectory acceptance mode
body:
## Summary

Adds an **`agentic`** eval mode that measures speculative-decoding acceptance across realistic long, multi-turn *agentic coding* contexts, using [ThoughtWorks' agentic-coding-trajectories](https://huggingface.co/datasets/thoughtworks/agentic-coding-trajectories) as the source.

> **Stacked on #1107.** This branch sits on top of `feat/long-context-acceptance`; since that branch isn't on this repo yet, the PR targets `main`, so the diff currently also shows #1107's commits. **Review only the last commit** (`feat(eval): add agentic-coding-trajectory acceptance mode`) here — merge #1107 first, then this rebases cleanly onto `main`.

It reuses the three-layer architecture from #1107 unchanged — generic `request_runner` (Parquet recording) + `acceptance_report` (analysis/binning) — and adds only a thin dataset adapter, `agentic.py`, mirroring `mrcr.py`.

### The replay

A session is a message list (system prompt, user task, then an alternation of model responses and tool/user turns). The *model responses* are exactly the `assistant` messages X1, X2, …; each is regenerated from its exact ground-truth prefix:

```
request i:  messages[:idx_i]  ->  regenerate X_i
```

This is framework-agnostic (swe-agent, mini-swe-agent, OpenHands, … all reduce to "which messages are the model's own"). Correctness is not graded — the trajectories are used only as a source of long, realistic contexts.

### Why no per-length binning (unlike MRCR)

A single trajectory **self-sweeps** context length: every response is replayed from a longer prefix than the last. So a flat sample of whole sessions already spans the context range, and no stratification is needed. Selection is a deterministic flat sample ranked by a stable content hash (pseudo-random but reproducible); per-response render fit-testing keeps the kept set **superset-monotone** in `max_model_len`.

### KV-cache locality

Within a session the replay prefixes are *nested*, so all of a session's replays go in the **same batch** and share the server's automatic prefix cache; whole sessions are packed into waves of ~`max_concurrency` (never split). Measured ~40–44% prefix-cache hit rate on 100k+ prefixes. For hybrid Mamba + MTP targets (e.g. Qwen3.5-4B) this needs dense retention (`--prefix-cache-retention-interval <block_size>` on older builds; default in vLLM 0.29) — documented in the module docstring.

### CLI

```bash
python evaluate.py --target http://localhost:8000/v1 agentic \
    --num-sessions 16 \
    --max-responses-per-session 6 \
    --min-session-tokens 100000
```

New flags (agentic mode): `--num-sessions`, `--max-responses-per-session`, `--max-new-tokens`, `--min-session-tokens` (sample only trajectories whose dataset token count is ≥ this, so runs reach high context lengths). `--selection-seed` / `--position-bin-size` are shared with long-context. `throughput`/`sweep` are unchanged and don't import the agentic deps.

### plot.py fixes (surfaced while validating)

- Adaptive k-axis labels: whole-k rounding collapsed adjacent log-spaced edges (e.g. 1038 and 1456 both → `1k`); now one decimal below 10k.
- The mean-accept-len line breaks over empty bins (NaN) instead of plunging to 0, which read as a false acceptance dip.

### Validation

- `pytest tests/unit/scripts/test_agentic.py` → **9 passed** (message reconstruction, even-spaced response thinning, wave packing, request building).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all four changed files.
- End-to-end against two servers: **Qwen3.5-4B + MTP** (hybrid Mamba, retention workaround) and **Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 + a dflash speculator** (256k context). A `--min-session-tokens 100000` run replayed 96 responses across 16 trajectories and swept context to **~125k tokens**, showing mean accept length decaying ~3.2 → ~2.1 as context grows.

### Non-duplication

No overlap with #1107's harness/report code — this only adds `agentic.py`, its unit test, the agentic flags in `evaluate.py`, and two label/line fixes in `plot.py`.
